arxiv-1903-10915.title: Language Model Adaptation for Language and Dialect Identification of Text
arxiv-1903-10915.description: Abstract This article describes an unsupervised language model adaptation approach that can be used to enhance the performance of language identification methods. The approach is applied to a current version of the HeLI language identification method, which is now called HeLI 2.0. We describe the HeLI 2.0 method in detail.

arxiv-2107-05628.title: Unconventional thermal and magnetic-field-driven changes of a bipartite entanglement of a mixed spin-(1/2, S S ) Heisenberg dimer with an uniaxial single-ion anisotropy
arxiv-2107-05628.creator: Hana Vargová 1, and Jozef Strečka 2
arxiv-2107-05628.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hana Vargová 1, and Jozef Strečka 2. The concept of negativity is adapted in order to explore the quantum and thermal entanglement of the mixed spin-(1/2, S S ) Heisenberg dimers in presence of an external magnetic field. The mutual interplay between the spin size S S , XXZ exchange and uniaxial single-ion anisotropy is thoroughly examined with a goal to tune the degree and thermal stability of the pairwise entanglement.

arxiv-2108-00318.title: Statistical learning method for predicting density-matrix based electron dynamics
arxiv-2108-00318.creator: Prachi Gupta, Harish S. Bhat, Karnamohit Ranka, Christine M. Isborn
arxiv-2108-00318.description: Abstract We develop a statistical method to learn a molecular Hamiltonian matrix from a time-series of electron density matrices. We extend our previous method to larger molecular systems by incorporating physical properties to reduce dimensionality, while also exploiting regularization techniques like ridge regression for addressing multicollinearity.

arxiv-2303-08672.title: Soft Fluidic Closed-Loop Controller for Untethered Underwater Gliders Thanks: 1 Department of Robotics Engineering, Worcester Polytechnic Institute, 100 Institute Road, Worcester, MA 01609, USA. 2 Department of Mechanical Engineering, Worcester Polytechnic Institute, 100 Institute Road, Worcester, M
arxiv-2303-08672.creator: Kalina Bonofiglio, Lauryn Whiteside, Maya Angeles, Matthew Haahr, Brandon Simpson, Josh Palmer, Yijia Wu, Markus P. Nemitz
arxiv-2303-08672.description: Abstract Soft underwater robots typically explore bio-inspired designs at the expense of power efficiency when compared to traditional underwater robots, which limits their practical use in real-world applications. We leverage a fluidic closed-loop controller to actuate a passive underwater glider. A soft hydrostatic pressure sensor is configured as a bang-bang controller actuating a swim bladder made from silicone balloons.

arxiv-2410-03487.title: A Multimodal Framework for DeepFake Detection
arxiv-2410-03487.creator: Kashish Gandhi, Prutha Kulkarni, Taran Shah*, Piyush Chaudhari*, Meera Narvekar, Kranti Ghag
arxiv-2410-03487.description: Abstract The rapid advancement of deepfake technology poses a significant threat to digital media integrity. Deepfakes, synthetic media created using AI, can convincingly alter videos and audio to misrepresent reality. This creates risks of misinformation, fraud, and severe implications for personal privacy and security.

pmc-12626016.title: Microfluidic networks using isotachophoresis
pmc-12626016.creator: Alexandre S. Avaro, Shahab Mirjalili, Andrew D. Griffiths, Juan G. Santiago
pmc-12626016.description: SignificanceMicrofluidic systems have revolutionized a great variety of chemical and biological processes and assays. Here, we introduce a type of microfluidic network based on an electrokinetic process called isotachophoresis (ITP).
